How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (8)

  1. How many employees does Lasso Security have, and how many work in engineering and customer support?
    Headcount indicates capacity to support enterprise customers.
  2. Has Lasso Security made any workforce reductions since it was founded?
    Layoffs can signal financial stress or reduced support capacity.
  3. Is Lasso Security party to any material litigation?
    Material litigation can affect a small supplier's finances.
  4. Has Lasso Security had any security incident affecting its systems or customer data, and how was it disclosed?
    A security supplier's own incident record is central to trust.
  5. Have any significant customers stopped using Lasso Security, and why?
    Loss of reference customers can signal product or service problems.
  6. Have there been any founder or executive departures or conduct issues at Lasso Security?
    Leadership conduct or instability is a reputational risk factor.
  7. What is Lasso Security's pricing metric and list price for each platform module?
    Without a pricing model a bank cannot budget or compare suppliers.
  8. What does a typical enterprise deployment of the Lasso platform cost per year?
    Without price points a bank cannot budget or compare suppliers.

Timeline

  1. 2026-09-02 · funding Lasso Security
    Lasso Security raises $30 million in round led by ClearSky

    SiliconANGLE reported on 2026-09-02, and SecurityBrief on 2026-09-08, that Lasso Security raised $30 million in a round led by ClearSky, with Entrée Capital (which led the 2023 seed round), iAngels, Singtel Innov8, Mindset and Swish Data. Neither report named the stage. SiliconANGLE put total funding at more than $37 million. The company said revenue had grown more than 500% in twelve months, without giving a figure. SiliconANGLE (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)SecurityBrief UK (TechDay) (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-09-02 · launch Lasso Security
    Lasso Security launches LEAP, a guardrail engine that runs on CPUs

    Alongside its funding round, Lasso launched LEAP, a guardrail engine that the company says runs on ordinary server CPUs and returns a verdict in under five milliseconds. It works with RAPID, a self-hosted model that handles the decisions needing judgement against a plain-language policy. Performance figures are the company's own and were not independently tested in the reports retrieved. SiliconANGLE (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)SecurityBrief UK (TechDay) (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)
